newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 22.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* LG&E Energy has agreed to acquire KU Energy for about $1.43 billion in a stock swap.
* The European Commission has formally challenged Boeing's plan to acquire McDonnell Douglas.
* The government posted a record $93.94 billion surplus in April.
* The U.S. trade deficit fell to a seasonally adjusted $8.51 billion in March.
* Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin urged Congress to remove barriers between banks, brokerage firms and insurance companies.
* The Dow Jones industrials dropped 12.77 to 7290.69 points.
* Brokerage-house stock pickers lost 0.4 percent on average for investors who followed their advice during the first quarter, according to a study by the Journal and Zacks.
* Big Board short interest rose 4.2 percent to 3.28 billion shares.
* Microsoft announced more than a dozen business information partners for its "push" technology.
* Intel Chief Operating Office Craig Barrett was named to the added post of president and Chief Executive Andrew Grove became chairman.
* AT&T Chairman Robert Allen sought to reassure stockholders, saying the company's stock remains undervalued and should be expected to rise.
* American International Group named Evan Greenberg president and operating chief.
* Ralph Lauren and his family could pull in close to $397 million if Polo Ralph Lauren succeeds in its previously proposed initial public offering.
* Broadcast-television viewership continued its slide in the eight-month season that ended Wednesday night.

* Heard on the Street: Not so long ago, corporate treasurers who used company resources to buy or sell stock options, in a bet that the company's stock would rise, would have been called gamblers or worse.

* Credit Markets: Treasury-bond prices fell sharply, undercut by renewed concern over the strength of the economy, doubts over the Federal Reserve's continuing ability to keep inflation under wraps and rumors of large sellers of government securities.
